ratings_why.fun: Routing Age with bats and dormice gives real choices each turn and the late thresholds land well, but the Long Sleep build is mostly waiting.
ratings_why.distinct: Age you can move and spend is a step past Hedgerow folk's turns-in-slot clocks, yet at a glance 'leave it alone and it grows' reads as the same idea.

verdict_why: Lamplighter Hrošč and Echo Bat each have a rules question a player can't answer from the card; both are one-line wording fixes.

points.text: Lamplighter Hrošč says Awaken 'doesn't change', but Clutch-Sister's +4/+4 and Dripstone Sleeper's +2/+2 are stats from Age. Say plainly whether Awaken payoffs are doubled.
Age is lost when a unit is sold, and Echo Bat gives a sold unit's Age away. Say the Bat moves the Age before it is lost.
Oldest and youngest drive Cloister Novice, Beehive Painter and Echo Bat; a fixed crown and seedling marker on the board would make the chain readable at a glance.
Cloister Warden's golden text ('they gain 2 Age from Still') reads like a different card; 'and their Still gives 2 Age' would match the normal text.

standouts.why: Brother Netopir is the bat courier as a rule: he carries Age from one side to whoever was played last, and the board shows who gets it.
Parkelj the Dark breaks the tribe's one rule, the scandal who moves, and the text is one short line.
Seven-Month Dormouse turns long sleep into gold in a line anyone can read.

weakest.why: Mother Ribica's step rule (2N, 3N, once a turn, missed steps wait) is the longest text in the tribe and hard to track across seven units.
Kurent Bellman is a flat number tweak; the carnival bell-ringer's fantasy doesn't come through in what it does.

flags.note: Whether Awaken stat payoffs are doubled can't be read from the card.
Timing against 'Age is lost when sold' isn't stated.
Golden Netopir copies Age from nothing; with golden Echo Bat and Ribica it could feed thresholds every turn.
Awaken 20 doubles the whole board permanently, and golden triples it; worth the owner's eye with Netopir relays.
